html:
A novel by José Rizal, written in Spanish and published in Berlin in 1887, that laid bare the abuses of Spanish rule in the Philippines. The Latin title means "touch me not", words of Jesus in the Gospel of John.

The hero, Crisóstomo Ibarra, comes home from Europe full of plans to build a school. He finds that his father died in prison after a quarrel with a powerful friar, and he is drawn into the plots of the parish priests and colonial officials. Around him Rizal sets a whole society: greedy clergy, cruel police, a mother driven mad by grief, a rebel boatman who has given up on reform.

The book did not call for revolution. It asked for honest government and limits on the friars. Still, the authorities of Spain banned it, and copies were smuggled in. Its sequel, El filibusterismo (1891), was angrier.

The two novels shaped a Filipino sense of nation and helped stir the Philippine Revolution. Since 1956 every Filipino high school student has had to read them.
